# demo_accel registers

Control and status of a stream accelerator with a descriptor ring and one interrupt. It follows the house register conventions (docs/hwsw.md); the Behaviour section states each one.

AXI4-Lite, 32-bit registers, a 0x1000-byte window (address bits [11:2] decoded). Unmapped addresses answer OKAY and read 0. Version 0.1.0; model sha256 `ab8f2adf0f98e7b6`.

## Register map

| Offset | Register | Reset | Summary |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0x000 | ID | 0x64a00100 | Block identity; software checks it before touching anything else. |
| 0x004 | CTRL | 0x01000020 | Configuration; written while the block is idle. |
| 0x008 | CMD | 0x00000000 | Commands; reading returns 0. |
| 0x00c | STATUS | 0x00000000 | Live state, read from the hardware. |
| 0x010 | IRQ_STATUS | 0x00000000 | Interrupt causes; write 1 to clear. |
| 0x014 | IRQ_ENABLE | 0x00000000 | Interrupt enables, bit for bit with IRQ_STATUS. |
| 0x020 | RING_BASE | 0x00000000 | Physical address of the descriptor ring (64-byte aligned). |
| 0x024 | RING_TAIL | 0x00000000 | Producer index, written by software after it fills descriptors. |
| 0x028 | RING_HEAD | 0x00000000 | Consumer index, advanced by the hardware. |
| 0x02c | DOORBELL | 0x00000000 | Per-queue doorbells; software rings, the hardware clears when it has seen the new tail. |
| 0x030 | JOB_CYCLES_LO | 0x00000000 | Clocks spent on jobs since reset, bits 31-0 (snapshot JOB_CYCLES). |
| 0x034 | JOB_CYCLES_HI | 0x00000000 | Clocks spent on jobs since reset, bits 63-32 (snapshot JOB_CYCLES). |
| 0x0fc | SCRATCH | 0x00000000 | Free read/write word for bus tests. |

Reset is what a read returns after reset with every hardware input low.

## Access types

| Access | Meaning |
|---|---|
| RW | read/write: software writes the value; hardware sees it on an output |
| RO | read-only: the value comes from a hardware input (or is a constant); writes are ignored |
| W1C | write 1 to clear: hardware sets bits with a pulse input; software clears a bit by writing 1 to it; a set and a clear in the same clock leave the bit set (no event is lost) |
| W1S | write 1 to set: software sets bits by writing 1 (a doorbell); hardware clears them with a pulse input; a set and a clear in the same clock leave the bit set |
| W1P | write 1 to pulse: each bit written as 1 gives a one-clock pulse on an output; reads return 0 |

## Behaviour

- **Unmapped addresses.** An address inside this block's 0x1000-byte window that holds no register answers OKAY and reads 0; a write there is ignored. Addresses outside the window belong to the interconnect (an AXI crossbar answers DECERR there).
- **Reserved bits.** Bits that belong to no field read 0 and ignore writes. Write them as 0, so that a later version can give them a meaning.
- **Reads have no side effects.** Reading any register changes nothing, so a debugger, a retried read or a read-modify-write is safe. To start, pop or acknowledge something, write 1 to its W1P bit: CMD.START, CMD.FLUSH, CMD.SNAP.
- **Same-clock priority (the house convention).** W1C bits (CTRL.OVERFLOW, IRQ_STATUS.DONE, IRQ_STATUS.ERROR): a hardware set in the same clock as a software clear wins, so the bit stays set and no event is lost. W1S bits (DOORBELL.QUEUE): a software set in the same clock as a hardware clear wins, so the set is not lost.
- **Partial writes.** Byte strobes (WSTRB) are honoured on every register: a byte whose strobe is 0 keeps its value, and in it W1C, W1S and W1P bits count as 0 (nothing is cleared, set or pulsed).
- **Access width and alignment.** 32-bit registers on a 32-bit AXI4-Lite bus. AXI4-Lite has no transfer size: a CPU's byte or halfword load reads the whole word, and its store arrives as a word write with fewer strobes (see Partial writes). Address bits [1:0] are not decoded, so an unaligned address reaches the word that holds it; only bits [11:2] are decoded, so the window repeats every 0x1000 bytes. Use aligned 32-bit accesses.
- **Values wider than 32 bits.** Snapshot group JOB_CYCLES (64 bits: JOB_CYCLES_LO.VALUE, then JOB_CYCLES_HI.VALUE, low part first): write 1 to CMD.SNAP to copy the whole value into shadow registers in one clock, then read the parts in any order; they belong to the same instant. A read without a new snapshot returns the copy from the last one (stale), not the live value; the copies read 0 after reset. Every other register is read on its own, so a value split across two of them can tear.
- **Reset.** `aresetn`, synchronous, active low (sampled on the rising edge of `aclk`). Every stored field takes the reset value in its table; W1P bits read 0; snapshot copies read 0. Not reset by this block: the RO fields that read a hardware input (STATUS.BUSY, STATUS.LEVEL, RING_HEAD.INDEX); they show their input's value.
- **Interrupt.** `irq_o` is a level output from a register: high while any bit of IRQ_STATUS (DONE, ERROR) is set together with the same bit of IRQ_ENABLE. Clear the cause by writing 1 to its IRQ_STATUS bit (W1C); the line falls one clock after the clear takes effect. A clear never loses a new event (a hardware set in the same clock wins), but events of the same cause between the handler's read and its clear merge into one: count them elsewhere if each one matters. Clear the cause before unmasking the line at the interrupt controller.
- **Clock domain and timing.** Every field is in the `aclk` domain; hardware inputs must be synchronous to `aclk` (the block has no synchronisers). A write takes effect on the hardware in the clock its write response (BVALID) is raised, and a W1P pulse is high for exactly that clock. A read returns the hardware's values as they were in the clock the read address was accepted.

## ID (0x000)

Block identity; software checks it before touching anything else.

| Bits | Field | Access | Reset | Summary |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 31:16 | MAGIC | RO const | 0x64a0 | fixed pattern 0x64A0 |
| 15:0 | VERSION | RO const | 0x100 | register-map version 1.0 |

## CTRL (0x004)

Configuration; written while the block is idle.

| Bits | Field | Access | Reset | Summary |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 27:16 | SCALE | RW | 0x100 | output gain, unsigned 4.8 fixed point |
| 8 | OVERFLOW | W1C | 0x0 | an input beat arrived while the block was disabled |
| 6:4 | MODE | RW | 0x2 | kernel select |
| 0 | ENABLE | RW | 0x0 | 1 lets the block accept stream data |

## CMD (0x008)

Commands; reading returns 0.

| Bits | Field | Access | Reset | Summary |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2 | SNAP | W1P | 0 | copy JOB_CYCLES (both halves) into its shadow registers |
| 1 | FLUSH | W1P | 0 | drop buffered data |
| 0 | START | W1P | 0 | start one job |

## STATUS (0x00c)

Live state, read from the hardware.

| Bits | Field | Access | Reset | Summary |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 15:8 | LEVEL | RO | hw | input FIFO fill in beats |
| 0 | BUSY | RO | hw | a job is running |

## IRQ_STATUS (0x010)

Interrupt causes; write 1 to clear.

| Bits | Field | Access | Reset | Summary |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | ERROR | W1C | 0x0 | a descriptor was malformed |
| 0 | DONE | W1C | 0x0 | a job finished |
